skill.name: set-up-woocommerce-meta-returning-customer-bidding
skill.description: Use Product Metrics to set up Meta bidding for paid repeat WooCommerce orders. Verify revenue or profit events before choosing a custom conversion for a retention campaign.
skill.summary: Set up and verify a Meta conversion for paid repeat WooCommerce orders.
skill.author: product-metrics

security_audit.summary: Most static alerts describe Markdown formatting, documentation links, or application setup rather than shell evaluation or host reconnaissance. The workflow directs authenticated reads, and its optional installer can fetch and execute unpinned code. No evidence of malicious intent was found, but the instructions risk exposing credentials, retrieving excess order data, importing history without approval, and misdirecting bidding.

remediation.issue: The Meta access token can enter the assistant session or command arguments.
remediation.suggestion: Remove the credential exception and require token entry in the Product Metrics app. Verify the destination using only redacted status.

remediation.issue: Setup status is read before the intended account is verified, and order checks may return more data than needed.
remediation.suggestion: Confirm the workspace, property, and storefront before authenticated reads. Use a bounded classification query and report only classifications or counts without customer or margin details.

remediation.issue: The install example uses an unpinned package runner and repository.
remediation.suggestion: Pin both the installer version and skill revision. Require explicit approval before installation and prefer an already trusted client for setup checks.

remediation.issue: The WooCommerce setup guide moves from a configuration check to an initial order import without a separate review.
remediation.suggestion: Explain which historical data goes to Product Metrics and which events go to Meta. Confirm the scope and merchant approval before the initial import.

remediation.issue: The root guide gives the general profit event as the example for a returning customer goal.
remediation.suggestion: Use the returning customer profit event and its matching purpose rule. Verify the event and rule before the merchant changes the ad set.

semantic_findings.title: Meta Access Token Can Enter the Assistant Session
semantic_findings.description: The skill exempts Meta access tokens from its rule against requesting secrets. The reference says to enter the token in the app but also tells the assistant to ask for it. This can expose the credential through conversation history, tool input, or process arguments.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The credential exception and instruction to ask for the token are explicit. No evidence of a secure agent input channel was found.

semantic_findings.title: Order Validation Retrieves More Data Than Needed
semantic_findings.description: The validation asks for new or returning classifications, but the prescribed order detail read also exposes order margins. The skill provides no instruction to limit returned fields or redact those margins.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The reference requests classification only, while the skill explicitly says the detail call returns margin. No other exposed fields were verified.

semantic_findings.title: Initial Order Import Lacks a Separate Data Review
semantic_findings.description: The WooCommerce guide tells the merchant to queue an initial order import after a configuration check. It does not explain the import scope when asking the merchant to start it. This can transfer more sales and customer records to Product Metrics than the merchant expects from a Meta test.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The guide explicitly queues an initial import and describes customer and cost data. The files do not specify the historical range of the import.

semantic_findings.title: Profit Example Can Optimize for the Wrong Orders
semantic_findings.description: The main skill uses the general order profit event as its profit example. The repeat-order guide specifies a different event and rule. Following the general example can make a retention campaign optimize for orders beyond repeat purchases.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The main skill names PMOrderProfit, while the repeat-order guide requires PMReturningCustomerProfit with a different purpose rule.

content.user_title: Set Up Meta Bidding for Repeat WooCommerce Orders
content.value_statement: A general purchase conversion does not distinguish repeat WooCommerce orders from first purchases. Use Product Metrics to verify repeat-order events and set up a Meta conversion that values revenue or profit.
actual_capabilities: Check setup status through the Product Metrics CLI or MCP when authenticated access is available.
Guide the merchant through connecting the WooCommerce plugin and the Meta Conversions API destination.
Check recent order classifications and explain how paid statuses, customer accounts, and guest billing emails affect them.
Identify the Meta custom conversion event and rule for repeat-order revenue or profit.
Guide verification of repeat test order delivery and distinguish test mode from live sending.
limitations: Setup requires a Product Metrics Pro workspace, a compatible WooCommerce store, and access to the intended Meta dataset.
The merchant creates the Meta custom conversion and selects it as the ad set optimization event.
Repeat-order custom events require marketing and analytics consent. Profit events also require complete cost data.
The integration does not import historical orders into Meta or revise repeat conversions after refunds.

use_cases.title: Check readiness for repeat-order tracking
use_cases.description: Find which WooCommerce, Product Metrics, and Meta prerequisites are in place before you test an event.

use_cases.title: Prepare a retention campaign
use_cases.description: Select a revenue or profit conversion and verify its rule before you change a Meta ad set.

use_cases.title: Diagnose a missing repeat conversion
use_cases.description: Check the paid status, customer match, consent, and event delivery for an approved test order.

prompt_templates.title: List setup requirements
prompt_templates.scenario: First setup for a WooCommerce store
prompt_templates.prompt: List the prerequisites for repeat-order bidding in Meta through Product Metrics. Use the documentation only and do not connect any accounts.

prompt_templates.title: Check existing setup
prompt_templates.scenario: A store is already linked to Product Metrics
prompt_templates.prompt: Confirm which workspace and storefront to check before reading setup status. Report the remaining steps without making changes or requesting tokens.

prompt_templates.title: Diagnose a missing event
prompt_templates.scenario: A repeat test order did not appear in Meta
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me check paid status, repeat classification, consent, and Meta test delivery for my test order. Do not show customer identifiers or margins.

prompt_templates.title: Review a profit conversion before launch
prompt_templates.scenario: A retention campaign will optimize for repeat-order profit
prompt_templates.prompt: Verify the proposed Meta event and rule for repeat-order profit. Check cost readiness and test delivery, then list the manual ad set changes for approval.

output_examples.input: Why does my repeat purchase event not appear in Meta?
output: Meta lists the repeat event after it receives it once.
Check that the test is a second paid order and has both marketing and analytics consent.
Look for the event in Test events, then remove the test code before starting live delivery.

output_examples.input: Which conversion should my repeat-order profit campaign use?
output: Use PMReturningCustomerProfit, not the general order profit event.
Set the event purpose to CUSTOMER_RETURNING_PROFIT and use the value and currency from the event.
Verify a repeat test order with complete costs before selecting the conversion in your ad set.

best_practices: Confirm the workspace, storefront, Meta dataset, and permission to share order data before connecting or importing.
Enter tokens only in the respective application. Keep customer identifiers and margins out of assistant summaries.
Verify a consented repeat test order before changing bidding. Remove the test code before checking live delivery.
anti_patterns: Pasting a store setup token or Meta access token into chat.
Using the general order profit event for a campaign that should measure repeat-order profit only.
Changing ad set optimization before checking the event, rule, and value in Meta.

faq.question: What counts as a returning WooCommerce customer?
faq.answer: Product Metrics looks for an earlier order in a selected paid status. It uses the customer account or the guest billing email.

faq.question: Can a guest order count as a repeat purchase?
faq.answer: Yes. A guest can count as returning when an earlier paid guest order used the same billing email.

faq.question: What consent is required for repeat-order events?
faq.answer: The guide requires marketing and analytics consent. Meta receives hashed matching fields and can also receive browser and network data.

faq.question: What happens if costs are missing or an order makes a loss?
faq.answer: Incomplete costs prevent the profit event. A repeat order with a loss sends zero as its profit conversion value.

faq.question: Does the setup send old orders or adjust refunds in Meta?
faq.answer: No. Historical orders are not imported into Meta, and later refunds do not revise the repeat conversion.

faq.question: Does the assistant change the campaign conversion?
faq.answer: No. You create the custom conversion in Meta Events Manager and select it in the ad set. The skill guides and verifies those steps.
